steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock. Replace all parts and panels before operating.

steps.title: Basket turns freely
steps.body: Manually check that the basket turns freely. Mechanical lockup must be resolved before electrical testing.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Check to see if basket will turn freely. If basket does not turn freely, determine what is causing the mechanical friction or lockup.

branches.label: Basket does not turn freely
branches.oemOutcome: Resolve mechanical friction or lockup before repeating motor circuit test.

steps.title: Mechanical lockup
steps.oemOutcome: Determine and correct mechanical friction or lockup; then repeat TEST #3 from step 1.

steps.title: Access ACU and verify J6
steps.body: Remove the top to access the ACU. Perform TEST #1 ACU power check, then verify connector J6 is fully seated in the ACU. Disconnect the motor harness from the ACU before resistance checks.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove the top to access the ACU. Perform TEST #1: ACU Power Check, then visually check that connector J6 is inserted all the way into the ACU. Check the motor windings — disconnect the motor harness from the ACU.

steps.title: Motor windings J6 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: With an ohmmeter at the motor harness disconnected from the ACU, measure resistance between J6 pins 1 (Motor U, BU) and 2 (Motor V, W). Wire colors are at the stator harness (J36) per Figure 2.
steps.sourceExcerpt: With an ohmmeter, verify the resistance values as shown: J6, Pins 1 & 2 — 6–20 Ω.

steps.title: Motor windings J6 pins 2 & 3
steps.body: Measure resistance between J6 pins 2 and 3.

steps.title: Motor windings J6 pins 1 & 3
steps.body: Measure resistance between J6 pins 1 and 3.
steps.sourceExcerpt: J6, Pins 1 & 3 — 6–20 Ω. If values are outside the range or open, replace stator assembly; otherwise reconnect the motor harness and go to step 7.

steps.title: Replace stator assembly
steps.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly. Reassemble, restore power, and run Quick Service Cycle to verify repair.

steps.title: Reconnect harness and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect the motor harness to the ACU. Reinstall panels as needed. Plug in or restore power. Door must be closed and locked before any motor test.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Plug in washer or reconnect power. IMPORTANT: Door must be closed and locked to run motor.

steps.title: Console control panel?
steps.body: Console models use membrane buttons and a seven-segment display. LCD-in-door models use the TOOLS menu and touchscreen — answer No for those.

steps.title: Console — enter Service Diagnostic mode
steps.body: Washer in standby (plugged in, indicators off). Wait 30 seconds after applying power. Choose any three buttons except POWER and remember them. Within 8 seconds, press and release button 1, then 2, then 3 — repeat that same 3-button sequence two more times (3 rounds total). Success: all console indicators illuminate for 5 seconds and the seven-segment display shows 888.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Select any three (3) buttons (except POWER)... Press and Release the 1st, 2nd, 3rd selected button; Repeat this 3 button sequence 2 more times. If entered successfully, all indicators are illuminated for 5 seconds with 888 showing in the display.

steps.title: Console — run Quick Service Cycle
steps.body: Press the 2nd button used to enter Service Diagnostic mode (momentary). Display should show 001. Use Soil to increment or Temp to decrement until function 012 (Quick Service Cycle) is selected. Press START — display flashes 012 while the cycle runs (drum must be empty). During the cycle, watch for display 009 and 013 — motor should run at spin (step 9) and tumble (step 13). Exit with POWER or hold the 1st diagnostic button for 5 seconds.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Press and release the 2nd button used to activate Service Diagnostic mode... Use Soil and Temp buttons to select function 012 Quick Service Cycle... Press START... display will flash 012 while the cycle runs. When the test shows 009 & 013 on the display, the motor is powered and the motor should be moving.

steps.title: LCD — enter Service Diagnostic mode
steps.body: Washer in standby. Open and close the door. Press POWER until the home screen displays. Press TOOLS → scroll to INFO → SERVICE & SUPPORT. Press and hold DIAGNOSTICS until ENTER PASSWORD appears. Enter 123, 123, 123 and press ENTER. On the warning screen, touch ENTER to reach DIAGNOSTICS HOME.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Press the TOOLS button. From the TOOLS menu, scroll down to INFO. From the INFO menu, select SERVICE & SUPPORT. Press and hold the DIAGNOSTICS button until ENTER PASSWORD is displayed. Input 123, 123, 123, and press ENTER.

steps.title: LCD — run Quick Service Cycle
steps.body: From DIAGNOSTICS HOME, scroll to Component Activation. Select Quick Service Cycle 1 and toggle ON (door will lock). Drum must be empty. During the cycle, verify motor runs at spin (step 9) and tumble (step 13). Toggle OFF when finished. Exit diagnostic mode: scroll to top, press < twice, then HOME.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Scroll down and select Component Activation... Turn Quick Service Cycle 1 On... When the test shows 009 & 013 on the display, the motor is powered and the motor should be moving.

steps.title: Motor movement during 009 & 013
steps.body: During Quick Service Cycle steps 9 (spin) and 13 (tumble), is the motor/drum moving?

branches.label: Motor is moving
branches.oemOutcome: Motor circuit OK — reassemble and verify with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.oemOutcome: Replace appliance control unit (ACU). Reassemble, restore power, and run Quick Service Cycle to verify repair.

steps.title: Repair verified
steps.oemOutcome: Disconnect power, reassemble all parts and panels, then run Quick Service Cycle to verify repair.
